newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN confirms at least 30,000 Kurds in Iran.
newsitem.headline: UN confirms at least 30,000 Kurds in Iran.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency said on Friday its staff had confirmed that 30,000 Kurds from northern Iraq were now in three sites in Iran, but said it did not expect the total exodus to exceed 40,000 people.
Spokesman Rupert Colville of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), also told a news briefing that UNHCR would soon send shelter material and other relief goods to Iran.
On Wednesday, Iran said it was sheltering 39,000 Kurdish refugees who fled the takeover this week of northern Iraq by a Baghdad-backed Kurdish faction.

"Our teams have now visited three major areas and verified the presence of 30,000 refugees," Colville told a news briefing. "We believe the region has 35,000 to 40,000, or more or less what the Iranian government said on Wednesday."
The spokesman said people were still crossing the border into Iran, while others were returning to Iraq's biggest Kurdish city Sulaimaniya, which fell on Monday. He had no figures.
"The biggest problem is mines," Colville said, referring to landmines along the military-sensitive border area. "A lot of displaced people are afraid to step off the road."
